rationale: The Court is likely to hold that enforceability of a broad appeal waiver turns on the Rule 11 knowing-and-voluntary inquiry and that a boilerplate Rule 32(j) advisement (and prosecutorial silence) ordinarily does not modify or nullify the waiver, which still bars due-process challenges to supervised-release conditions. Sotomayor and Jackson are likely to dissent on a narrow due-process/reliance theory that official, unqualified post-sentencing advice creates material ambiguity at the moment the defendant must decide whether to appeal.
